title: Heuristics and Biases
welcome_lead: People are not perfectly rational - Kahneman shows how.
meta_desc: A-Level Behavioural Economics: heuristics and biases.
final_note: Real decisions use shortcuts - and shortcuts have predictable biases.

walkthroughs.body_html: Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky showed in the 1970s that people use heuristics that systematically misjudge probability - winning Kahneman the 2002 Nobel.
System 1 is fast and intuitive - prone to bias. System 2 is slow and deliberate - but lazy. Many bad decisions happen when System 1 answers without consulting System 2.
Anchoring (a first number sticks), availability (vivid memories dominate), framing (gain vs loss wording), and confirmation (seeking agreeable evidence). Marketing exploits all four.

mcqs.q: What is asymmetric information as a source of market failure?
options: YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
Asymmetric information means a buyer and seller disagree about a price.

When one party in a transaction knows more than the other — leading to problems like adverse selection (used-car market) or moral hazard (insurance). Markets can fail or unravel when information is unequal.

mcqs.q: What does Income Elasticity of Demand (YED) tell us?
options: A negative YED means the demand calculation went wrong.
The fiscal multiplier is the rate of growth of the money supply.
YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.
The sign tells us the good type: positive YED = normal good (rises with income); negative YED = inferior good (falls with income). YED > 1 indicates a luxury; YED between 0 and 1 a necessity.
